texts.preamble: Master Ankit vs . Gopal & Ors. on 1 April, 2023 :1: In The Court Sh. Naveen Kumar Kashyap Additional District And Sessions Judge Po Mact, South East District, Saket Courts: New Delhi Mact No.: 4054/16 Fir no. 779/2016 Ps Okhla Ind. Area Cnr No.: Dlse01-001495-2015 Master Ankit Vs. Gopal & ors. Master Ankit S/o Sh. Rakesh R/o A-263, Okhla, Phase-I, Benali Camp, Okhla Industrial Estate, New Delhi. Through his father Sh. Rakesh .....Petitioner/Claimant Versus 1. Sh. Gopal S/o Ram Singh R/o Juggi no. 52, Opp. A-229 Bangali Camp, Okhla Ph. 1, New Delhi. .....Driver/Respondent no.1 2. Pardeep Kumar S/o Sh. Nayan Singh A-42, Aiims Campus, Ayurvigyan, New Delhi. Mact No. 4054/16 Master Aniket v. Gopal & anr. Page No. 1 of 28 rpt :2: .......Owner/Respondent no.2 Date of accident : 19.10.2014 Date of filing of Dar : 10.03.2015 Master Ankit vs . texts.facts: This is one of the 20 oldest matters pending in this tribunal, hence taken on priority basis. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act on 10.03.2015 and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 19.10.2014 at about 5.10 PM, petitioner/injured was standing/playing in front of Jhuggi, Opp. Bengali Camp, A-263, Okhla Phase-I, New Delhi, suddenly motorcycle bearing no. UP-16B-3349 being driven rashly and negligently by its driver namely Gopal hit the petitioner. Due to such impact, he fell down and received grievous injuries. He was taken to Trauma Center, AIIMS, New Delhi where he remained hospitalized from 20.10.2014 to 03.01.2015. Thereafter, he was treated at Banarasidas Chandiwal Hospital, New Delhi. It is further claimed that he was of 5 years and was studying in LKG at the time of accident. It is further MACT No. 4054/16 Master Aniket v. Gopal & anr. Page No. 2 of 28 rp :3: stated that because of such rash and negligent act of respondent no.1, petitioner also suffered permanent disability and as such loss of future prospects. 3. Accordingly the FIR in question u/s 279/338 IPC was registered in this case and even chargesheet is filed. 4. Further, Medical Board of Jai Prakash Narayan Apex Trauma Center, AIIMS, New Delhi sent disability report dated 01.10.2021 noticing 100% permanent disability in relation to locomotor and neurological. 5. Further, as per record, initially R-1 driver Gopal and R-2 Pradeep Kumar appeared and said Pradeep Kumar told that the said offending vehicle has been sold by him to one Shubham Gupta, and said Shubham Gupta sold the same to Mohd. Salauddin and Mohd. Salauddin sold the same to Vinay Chaudhary and said Vinay Chaudhary sold to the driver/Gopal who is driver of said offending vehicle in question. Thereafter, R-2 Pradeep Kumar and R-4 Mohd. Salauddin appeared in court but R-1, R-3 and R-5 did not appear and proceeded ex-parte. However, R-2 Pradeep filed his written statement. on 1 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74232032/ 2 were framed on 02.07.2015 by Predecessor of this Tribunal: OPP. 2. To what amount of compensation the petitioner is entitled to claim and from whom? 3. Relief. MACT No. 4054/16 Master Aniket v. Gopal & anr. Page No. 3 of 28 rpt :4: 7. Further, as per record, Sh. Rakesh, father of injured/petitioner Master Ankit examined himself as PW-1. Such PW-1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary and medical bills etc. as Ex. PW-1/1 till Ex. PW-1/7. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for registered owner/R-2 Pradeep Kumar. 8. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 9 Vide order dated 10.02.2017, Driver/R-1 proceeded was ex-parte as he stopped appearing. 10. Further, owner Pradeep Kumar tendered his affidavit by way of evidence as R-2W-1/A. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for petitioner. 11. No other evidence has been led on behalf of respondents. 12. Thereafter, matter was adjourned sin-e-die for want of filing of disability certificate with liberty to petitioner to get the same revived as and when disability certificate is received. 13. Thereafter, vide order dated 11.01.2018, present matter was revived by my learned Predecessor. Further, Medical Superintendent was summoned for some clarifications regarding disability certificate. 14. Further, present matter was adjourned as sin-e-die vide order dated 11.03.2019 by my learned Predecessor as adjournment was sought on behalf of petitioner on the ground that petitioner needs to be re-examined after 2 years considering MACT No. 4054/16 Master Aniket v. Gopal & anr. Page No. 4 of 28 rpt :5: the disability certificate. Further, liberty was given to the petitioner to get the present petition revived after completion of two years and the file was consigned to record room. 15. Thereafter, as per record, an application u/s 151 CPC for revival of case was moved on 01.02.2021 and same was revived vide order dated 15.09.2022. Further, as per ordersheet dated 12.11.2021, Disability Certificate noticing 100 % permanent disability in relation to locomotor and neurological received. . In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal.
texts.arguments: In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 22. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of MACT No. 4054/16 Master Aniket v. Gopal & anr. Page No. 7 of 28 rpt :8: wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 27. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Master Ankit vs . Gopal & Ors. 5 Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. . It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Master Ankit vs . Gopal & Ors. 30. In Judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as "M. R. Krishna Murthi vs The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. on 5 March, 2019, (2020) 15 SCC 493: (2020) 4 SCC (Crl.) 84: 2019 SCC Online SC 315 , after dealing with various case laws relating to injury matters and death cases in case of students, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows: "24. In those cases where the victim of the accident is not an earning person but a student, while assessing the compensation for loss of future earning, the focus of the examination would be the career prospect and the likely earning of such a person in Master Ankit vs . Gopal & Ors. said course Further in the case of Kajal vs Jagdish Chand Civil Appeal No. 735 OF 2020, decided on 05.02.2020 by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, which is a case relating to injury to a minor child, inter alia Hon'ble Courts held: "......3. How does one assess compensation in such a case? No amount of money can compensate this child for the injuries suffered by her. She can never be put back in the same position. However, compensation has to be determined in terms of the provisions of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short the Act). The Act requires determination of payment of just compensation and it is the duty of the court to ensure that she is paid compensation which is just. . . They should not MACT No. 4054/16 Master Aniket v. Gopal & anr. Page No. 12 of 28 rpt be just token damages...." 32. In such case of Kajal (supra), Hon'ble Supreme Court further held : In M/s Concord of India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nirmala Devi and others, this Court held: "2....The determination of the quantum must be liberal, not niggardly since the law values life and limb in a free country in generous scales." 36. In the case of Kajal (supra), it was further held by Hon'ble Supreme Court: "Loss of earning. Each case has to be MACT No. 4054/16 Master Aniket v. Gopal & anr. Page No. 13 of 28 rpt decided on its own evidence but taking notional income to be Rs.15,000/ per annum is not at all justified. The appellant has placed Master Ankit vs . Gopal & Ors. on 1 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74232032/ 9 before us material to show that the minimum wages payable to a skilled workman is Rs.4846/ per month. Applying the multiplier of 18 it works out to Rs.14,65,430.40, which is rounded off to Rs.14,66,000/" 37. In this background, it is claimed by learned counsel for respondent side that there is no "loss of income" at present and further there is no loss of future prospect. It is further pointed out that normally in MACT claim, under other various heads, other than these two, suitable compensation can be given as per law. 38. On the other hand, it is argued by learned counsel for petitioner that there is 100% disability in relation to Locomotor and Neurological in the present case having regard to material on record and accordingly compensation be given for future prospect. 43. Regarding attendant charges, it is held in the case of Kajal (supra) by Hon'ble Supreme Court: "...Attendant charges 22. Multiplier system is used to balance out various factors..........." . . Master Ankit vs . Gopal & Ors. Regarding pain, suffering ad loss of amenities, it was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kajal (supra): "......Pain, Suffering and Loss of Amenities 26. Coming to the nonpecuniary damages under the head of pain, suffering, loss of amenities, the High Court has awarded this girl only Rs.3,00,000/. In Mallikarjun v. Divisional MACT No. 4054/16 Master Aniket v. Gopal & anr. Page No. 15 of 28 rpt Manager, The National Insurance Company Limited and Ors.14, this Court while dealing with the issue of award under this head held that it should be at least Rs.6,00,000/, if the disability is more than 90%. Further as also already held by this Tribunal during Master Ankit vs . Gopal & Ors. on 1 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74232032/ 14 proceedings of present case on 01.02.2023, that in the case of "Naveen Kumar vs. Vijay Kumar ((2018) 3 SCC 1), which is a three judges Bench judgment that too of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India where the law is well clarified for the purpose of present proceeding even after transferring/selling his vehicle to another person when his name is continued to be reflected in the record of registering authority as owner, such registered owner would continue to be treated as owner under MV Act and would not stand absolved of his liability as owner under the Act. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. "......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". However, in such cases, the Tribunal shall make sure that the amount is actually spent for the purpose and the MACT No. 4054/16 Master Aniket v. Gopal & anr. Page No. 22 of 28 rpt demand is not a ruse to withdraw money. In accordance with the orders dated 08.02.2019 MACT No. 4054/16 Master Aniket v. Gopal & anr. Page No. 26 of 28 rpt passed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in FAO no. 842/2003 in Rajesh Tyagi and others Vs.
